first: संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि ।
en: Arjuna said: Krishna, you praise giving up action, and then again the yoga of action. Tell me for certain which one of the two is better.
Krishna said: Giving up action and the yoga of action both lead to the highest good. But of the two, the yoga of action is better than giving up action.

first: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति ।
en: One who neither hates nor longs for anything should be known as one who has truly given up. Free from the pairs of opposites, mighty-armed one, such a person is easily freed from bondage.
Children, not the wise, say that Sankhya and Yoga are different. One who truly follows even one of them gains the result of both.
The state reached by the followers of Sankhya is also reached by the followers of Yoga. One who sees Sankhya and Yoga as one truly sees.
But giving up action is hard to reach without yoga, mighty-armed one. The sage who is steady in yoga soon reaches Brahman.
Steady in yoga, pure in heart, master of the self and of the senses, and seeing his own self as the self of all beings, such a person is not stained even while acting.
The one who knows the truth and is steady thinks, "I do nothing at all," even while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping and breathing;
while speaking, letting go, taking, opening and closing the eyes. Such a person holds that the senses are moving among their objects.

first: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः ।
en: One who acts while placing all actions in Brahman and giving up attachment is not stained by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water.
Yogis, giving up attachment, act with the body, the mind, the intellect, and even the senses alone, to make themselves pure.
The steady person, giving up the results of action, reaches lasting peace. The unsteady person, attached to results because of desire, is bound.
The self-controlled soul, giving up all actions with the mind, lives happily in the city of nine gates, the body, neither acting nor causing action.

first: न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः ।
en: The Lord does not create doership or actions for people, nor the link between action and result. It is nature that does this.

first: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः ।
en: The all-present one does not take on anyone's sin or good deeds. Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and so beings are confused.
But for those in whom this ignorance is destroyed by knowledge of the self, that knowledge lights up the Supreme like the sun.
With their understanding fixed on That, their self in That, their devotion in That, and That as their goal, their sins washed away by knowledge, they go where there is no return.
The wise see the same in a learned and humble Brahmin, in a cow, in an elephant, in a dog, and in one who eats dogs.

first: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः ।
en: Even here in this life, birth is conquered by those whose minds rest in sameness. Brahman is without fault and the same in all, so they rest in Brahman.
Steady in understanding, free from confusion, knowing Brahman and resting in Brahman, one should not rejoice on getting what is pleasant nor be upset on getting what is unpleasant.
One who is not attached to outer contacts finds the joy that is in the self. Joined to Brahman through yoga, such a person enjoys joy that does not end.

first: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते ।
en: Pleasures born of contact with the senses are sources of pain. They have a beginning and an end, son of Kunti. The wise do not delight in them.
One who can bear, here in this life before leaving the body, the force born of desire and anger is steady and happy.
One whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, and whose light is within, is a yogi. Becoming Brahman, such a person reaches the peace of Brahman.
Sages whose sins are destroyed, whose doubts are cut away, who are self-controlled and delight in the good of all beings, reach the peace of Brahman.
For those who strive, who are free from desire and anger and have controlled their minds and know the self, the peace of Brahman is near on every side.
Shutting out outside contacts, fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, and making the in-breath and out-breath move evenly through the nose;
the sage who controls the senses, mind and intellect, who aims at freedom, and from whom desire, fear and anger are gone, is truly free for ever.
Knowing me as the one who receives all sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all the worlds, and the friend of all beings, one reaches peace.
